location: Single click on a feed picture
issue: Single click on a picture cuts Program to it, breaking the macOS convention that a single click selects/focuses and an action needs an explicit control or a double-click. The same click also focuses the tile.
evidence: main-expanded legend 2: 'Click a picture or press ⌃1/⌃2 to cut'; monitor-tools keyboard card: 'Click a tile to focus it (blue ring)'; MonitorWorkspaceShell.swift surface(): .simultaneousGesture(TapGesture().onEnded { focusedTile = index }).
scenario: Mid-meeting the user clicks Feed 2 to adjust its zebra; Zoom cuts to Feed 2.
recommendation: Single click selects and focuses the feed. Make that the visible selected-feed state, which also resolves S2. Cut only from explicit controls: toolbar cut group, the strip's 'Cut to Feed N', ⌃1–⌃4 and the Program menu.
alternatives: Double-click to cut (HIG default-action pattern, still risky live)
Cut only from the cut bar in Program view
affects: menubar (thumbnails as cut buttons are acceptable: menus are explicit)

issue: The ⋯ popover is about 850 pt tall with six grouped sections, a file picker and a destructive Remove Camera. HIG reserves popovers for a small amount of transient content. A popover this size covers the pictures it configures and dismisses on any outside click.
evidence: main-collapsed: popover spans y≈80–950 of the 1170 desktop; sections Source, Processing, LUT, Recording, Output, Monitor; footer Rename…, Diagnostics…, Remove Camera.
scenario: The user opens ⋯ to load a LUT, the NSOpenPanel takes focus and the popover dismisses, losing context. Or they can't see the picture while toggling effects.
recommendation: Turn ⋯ into a Menu: Rename…, Load LUT…, Copy Monitor Settings To ›, Show Diagnostics, separator, Remove Camera… (role .destructive + confirmationDialog). Put the full per-feed form in an on-demand .inspector (macOS 14+) that's closed by default. This respects 'no inspector' as the resting state, keeps the pictures visible and survives file panels.
alternatives: A sheet per feed (modal, blocks monitoring)
Split into two small popovers: Processing+LUT, and Source+Recording

location: Picture tool buttons: settings via long-press / ⌥-click
issue: Tool settings open through long-press or ⌥-click on a toggle button. Neither is a macOS button convention, so the settings are undiscoverable. 'Hold Clean' press-and-hold has the same problem.
evidence: monitor-tools section header: 'click again or open its popover (long-press / ⌥-click) for settings'. Hold Clean in the overlay anatomy.
scenario: The user wants to change the zebra threshold and can't find how; the button only toggles.
recommendation: Use the native split pull-down: Menu(content:label:primaryAction:) (verified, macOS 12+). Clicking the face toggles the tool and the attached chevron opens its settings. Also put tool settings in the tile context menu and in View ▸ Monitor Tools ›. Keep Hold Clean as a keyboard hold (⌃⌥C held) with the toggle as the visible control.
alternatives: A single 'Tools' pull-down per picture listing all five with toggles and 'Settings…'

issue: The dropdown needs live video plus native menu rows. MenuBarExtra(.menu) can't host video, and .window (WindowMenuBarExtraStyle) loses real menu behavior. The recommended NSStatusItem + NSMenu + NSMenuItem.view is real AppKit API, but custom-view items get no keyboard highlight and don't auto-dismiss on click. The live layer also has to render during menu event tracking. Clickable cut thumbnails inside a view item are fully custom.
evidence: SDK: NSMenuItem.view (macos 10.5), subtitle (macos 14.4; shown on 15+), sectionHeaderWithTitle (14.0), badge (14.0) in NSMenuItem.h; WindowMenuBarExtraStyle in SwiftUI interface. menubar (a): 'thumbnails act as cut buttons'.
scenario: Implementation finds the preview frozen while the menu tracks, or arrow keys skip the cut thumbnails, so cuts can't be done from the keyboard.
recommendation: Spike first. Build rows natively: NSMenuItem.subtitle for 'Recording 12:31' (not inline gray text), sectionHeader for 'Cameras'/'Recording', badge for counts. Make cut targets regular NSMenuItems ('Cut to Feed 2 ⌃2') whose image is a still thumbnail refreshed at about 1 Hz, rather than live clickable views. Keep exactly one custom view: the preview.
alternatives: MenuBarExtra(.window) with hand-built menu-styled rows (easy video, custom keyboard nav and submenus)

issue: The Program and single-camera dropdowns are about 700–770 pt tall (preview 178, thumbnails ~110, ~21 rows × 25). On a 13" MacBook Air at the 'Larger Text' display setting (1024×640 pt), or on small external displays, NSMenu shows scroll arrows and the top custom preview item scrolls away.
evidence: menubar.png (a) spans y≈95–770 and (b) y≈95–785 at 1× points; the rows include separate Open Ultracam / Settings… / Quit plus a stat line.
scenario: A laptop user at larger text opens the menu and has to scroll to reach Stop Recording.
recommendation: Cap at about 12 top-level rows. Fold Effects/LUT/Input into the Feed N › submenu, put Pause and Show in Finder under Recording ›, and merge Open/Settings into the footer. Shrink the preview to 300×169 and drop the separate stat line (it's in the status bar and diagnostics).
alternatives: Collapse the preview to a 1-line status row when screen height < 800 pt

issue: The proposed red recording dot and orange attention dot break the template-image convention for status items and collide with the system privacy indicators (orange = microphone in use, green = camera in use).
evidence: menubar icon states: 'Recording red dot NEW', 'Attention orange dot NEW'; settings General 'Show attention dot for problems'.
scenario: The user sees an orange dot near the clock and thinks their microphone is live, or misses that the dot belongs to Ultracam.
recommendation: Keep the status item a template image. Show state through symbol variants (e.g. video.fill / arrow.right.square / a 'record' glyph badge / exclamationmark.triangle). If color is kept, use red for recording only and never orange.
alternatives: Monochrome badge dot (template) plus the accessibility label carrying the state

location: Status bar spanning beneath the floating sidebar
issue: The mockups draw a window-wide status bar with the floating glass sidebar ending above it. NavigationSplitView's macOS 26+ floating sidebar runs the full window height. A window-wide bottom bar under it isn't the native layout, and .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) on the split view may not produce it.
evidence: spec §1: 'Sidebar … ends 8 above status bar'; spec §4 status bar = .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom). Every main-window mockup shows the sidebar stopping at the bar.
scenario: Engineering builds it natively and the bar ends up only under the detail column or overlapping the sidebar, so the design doesn't match.
recommendation: Design the status bar in the detail column only (the sidebar keeps full height), applied to the detail view. Update measurements in spec §1. Verify in the window spike.
alternatives: A custom container instead of NavigationSplitView (loses native sidebar behavior)

issue: The toolbar carries title + cut group (3) + layout picker (4) + collapse toggle + record. At the specified 980 pt minimum it overflows into the » menu, which can hide live cut buttons. The record item shows only '12:31 · 2' with no verb. The collapse toggle uses a 'sliders' (adjust/filter) symbol with only a title attribute.
evidence: r3.js toolbar(): tb-btn title='Collapse strips' with ic('sliders'); prominent record shows `${recLabel}` only. spec §1 minimum 980×680.
scenario: At a small window size Feed 2's cut button goes into the overflow menu mid-meeting. The user can't tell whether the red '12:31 · 2' button stops everything.
recommendation: Give every ToolbarItem a Label (text + symbol) so Icon+Text mode and customization work. Set ToolbarItemVisibilityPriority (macOS 26, verified) high for cuts and record, low for layout and collapse. Label the record item 'Stop All' / 'Record All' with elapsed as secondary. Use a collapse symbol such as rectangle.compress.vertical.
alternatives: Move the layout picker into View menu / toolbar title menu (toolbarTitleMenu, macOS 13)

issue: Glass controls stay on the video permanently: identity, role, five tool buttons, timecode, signal picker, REC. Liquid Glass treats glass as a floating controls layer. Video players (AVKit/QuickTime) auto-hide chrome over content. Always-on glass over bright regions also loses legibility.
evidence: main-expanded: tool group top-right and TC/Output bottom-left on both pictures at rest. Only Four Up hides the tool group until hover.
scenario: Pills over the bright window region in the frame are hard to read, and they block framing checks.
recommendation: At rest show only identity + tally badge + REC. Reveal the tools, signal picker and TC on hover or keyboard focus (as Four Up already does). Group the pills in a GlassEffectContainer and use the opaque material under Reduce Transparency.
alternatives: Move the tool toggles into the strip header
Keep TC permanently only when Timecode is enabled in a View setting

issue: The sidebar is built as a NavigationSplitView source list but works as a control panel. Camera rows aren't selectable; it holds switches, a strategy pop-up, a shot timer and a Recover button. Sidebars in macOS denote navigation and selection, and VoiceOver announces them that way.
evidence: r3.js sidebar(): camera rows with no selection binding (first row has a static highlight); Auto switching switch, strategy popup, automation switches.
scenario: The user clicks Feed 2 in the sidebar expecting it to become the target of ⇧⌘B/Feed menu; nothing happens.
recommendation: Bind the Cameras List selection to selectedFeedID, which gives a visible selected feed (S2) and native keyboard selection. Keep Output/Recording/Takes as rows that open popovers or reveal in Finder. Move the set-once automation switches to the Feed/Record menus + Settings, leaving status in the sidebar.
alternatives: Keep it as a non-navigational leading panel (custom HStack) instead of NavigationSplitView

issue: ⌘0 is proposed twice: Window ▸ Ultracam (main window) in app-menus/spec, and 'Fit ⌘0' picture zoom in monitor-tools. ⌘= / ⌘− zoom appear only in monitor-tools: they're missing from the app-menus View menu and spec §6, and aren't marked NEW.
evidence: app-menus.html row('Ultracam', key '⌘0'); spec.html row ⌘0 Main window; monitor-tools.html keyrow '⌘ = ⌘ − Zoom in / out, ⌘0 to fit' and pill 'Fit ⌘0'.
scenario: The engineer implements both and one shortcut silently wins.
recommendation: Use View ▸ Zoom In ⌘= / Zoom Out ⌘− / Zoom to Fit ⌥⌘0 (or ⌘9), keep ⌘0 for the main window, and add them to app-menus and the spec table with the NEW tag.
alternatives: Drop ⌘0 for the main window (Window menu item without a shortcut)

issue: Quitting while recording is drawn as a sheet on the main window. In menu-bar-only mode (Hide from Dock, window closed), which is the common meeting setup, there's no window to attach a sheet to.
evidence: states §6 'Quit while recording' sheet over a window; UltracamApp.swift applicationShouldTerminate returns .terminateLater while recordings finish.
scenario: The user quits from the menu bar with the window closed; nothing visible explains why the app hasn't quit.
recommendation: Use an app-modal NSAlert (or a small standalone 'Finishing recordings' panel) when no main window is visible; use a sheet only when the window is open.
alternatives: Open the main window, then show the sheet

issue: Settings duplicates live view state that belongs in the View menu: Session sidebar Show/Hide (⌃⌘S) and Video preview (⇧⌘P). HIG keeps Settings for preferences, not toggles that change the current window.
evidence: settings General: 'Session sidebar  Show', 'Video preview' switch with ⇧⌘P.
scenario: The user toggles the preview in Settings and in the View menu, and can't tell which is authoritative.
recommendation: Remove both from Settings, or rephrase as launch defaults ('Show sidebar when the window opens').

issue: The destructive Remove Camera sits in a row next to Rename… and Diagnostics…, with no separation or confirmation. 'Diagnostics…' uses an ellipsis though it opens a window without asking for more input.
evidence: main-collapsed.html: Rename…Diagnostics… + red Remove Camera.
scenario: The user misclicks Remove Camera next to Diagnostics once the feed is stopped.
recommendation: Put destructive actions after a separator in a Menu with role .destructive and a confirmationDialog. Rename the window command 'Show Diagnostics' (no ellipsis).

issue: TabsPickerStyle / .pickerStyle(.tabs) is verified in MacOSX27.0.sdk (macOS 27.0), but its appearance is unverified. The mockups draw a segmented capsule, and the real control may render as a toolbar tab bar.
evidence: SDK: 'public struct TabsPickerStyle : SwiftUI.PickerStyle' @available(macOS 27.0); diagnostics.html tab control drawn as a segmented capsule.
scenario: The built Diagnostics window doesn't match the mockup, and its tabs land somewhere unexpected.
recommendation: Render .tabs in a scratch build before finalizing. Fall back to Picker(.segmented) in the principal toolbar item, the established pattern for switching a window among 2–4 peers.

issue: Effect chips (LUT/1080p/4:2:0/29.97) look like passive tags, not toggles. The round record button is custom-drawn. Neither is a native control as drawn, so toggle affordance, accessibility traits and keyboard activation have to be rebuilt.
evidence: r3.js fxChips() spans; .recbtn CSS circle; spec §4 maps chips to Toggle(.button).
scenario: The user doesn't realize tapping '4:2:0' changes what Zoom receives, or does it by accident thinking it's a label.
recommendation: Use Toggle with .toggleStyle(.button) inside a ControlGroup (bordered when on, with a help tag), and a Button with record.circle / stop.circle.fill symbols, tinted red with a glassProminent or bordered style. Native controls bring keyboard and VoiceOver support for free.
alternatives: Make chips read-only status and edit effects only in the Feed menu/inspector

issue: WindowGroup(for: MonitorTargetID.self) is buildable: the API is verified (macOS 13+) and MonitorTargetID is Hashable + Codable. But WindowGroup windows restore at relaunch by default, which would reopen monitor surfaces and start GPU work at launch.
evidence: SDK WindowGroup init<D,C>(id:for:) ; MonitorConfiguration.swift: struct MonitorTargetID: RawRepresentable, Hashable, Codable; restorationBehavior(_:) available macOS 15.
scenario: Ultracam launches in the menu bar and silently reopens two monitor windows from last session.
recommendation: Apply .restorationBehavior(.disabled) to the monitor WindowGroup (or decide restoration deliberately), and note it in spec §4/§9.

evidence: See L5-01: picture click is documented as both cut and focus; it violates the single-click-selects convention.
Sidebar camera rows aren't selectable (r3.js sidebar()), and only a static highlight on Feed 1 hints at selection; Feed menu header 'acts on Feed 1' in app-menus is the only explicit indicator.
note: Fix through native List selection (L5-10) and click-to-select (L5-01).

evidence: Five always-on tool buttons per picture on main pages; Four Up already shows the hover-reveal pattern.
⌘= / ⌘− / ⌘0 zoom in monitor-tools are untagged and collide with ⌘0 main window (L5-11).
note: Other inventions are left to L8.

evidence: Dropdowns are about 700–770 pt. They fit a default 13" (≈ 920 pt usable) but overflow at Larger Text (640 pt), where NSMenu scrolls away the custom preview item.
The toolbar record item is labelled only with elapsed time and a count; there's no verb (L5-08).
note: The strip and menu Stop wording is left to L7/L2.
